articles.title: Cratera em galeria exposta oferece risco de queda em Teresina | G1
articles.standfirst: Estrutura de laje está comprometida e pode ceder com a passagem de pedestres, segundo especialista. Moradores também relatam dificuldades. A SDU Sul foi procurada, mas não havia se manifestado até a publicação desta reportagem.
articles.summary: Estrutura de laje está comprometida e pode ceder com a passagem de pedestres, segundo especialista. Moradores também relatam dificuldades para atravessar o trecho.
articles.body:
Uma cratera aberta em uma galeria no cruzamento da Rua Álvaro Freire com a Avenida Odilon Araújo, no bairro Cristo Rei, Zona Sul de Teresina , corre risco de desabamento e oferece perigo para pedestres. A estrutura da laje que cobre parte da abertura está comprometida e, segundo avaliação do Conselho Regional de Engenharia e Agronomia do Piauí (CREA-PI), a recomendação é interdição imediata. Procurada, a SDU Sul ainda não se posicionou.

O especialista Cleitmã Oliveira recomendou o isolamento imediato do trecho até que sejam realizados os reparos necessários. Segundo ele, a estrutura perdeu a estabilidade e uma sobrecarga, como a passagem de uma ou mais pessoas, pode provocar o rompimento da laje.

“Como a laje já está com a sua estrutura comprometida, a estabilidade dela já não é mais garantida. Então existe o risco de a pessoa, passando por sobre essa laje, vir a romper e a pessoa sofrer uma queda para dentro da abertura da galeria”, explicou à TV Clube.

A reportagem procurou a Superintendência de Desenvolvimento Urbano (SDU) Sul para saber quais providências serão adotadas para solucionar o problema, mas o órgão não havia se manifestado até a publicação desta reportagem.

Além do risco de queda, o especialista apontou outros dois problemas: a dificuldade de circulação dos pedestres e o risco de atropelamento. Como a abertura ocupa parte da passagem, quem tenta atravessar o trecho pode precisar disputar espaço com os veículos na pista.

“O pedestre tem dificuldade de passar por sobre a calçada e, tendo dificuldade de passar por sobre a calçada, vem o terceiro risco, que é o risco de atropelamento, quando ele tem que se dirigir para a pista e disputar espaço com os carros num local de tráfego intenso”, afirmou.

Para o especialista, a primeira providência deve ser impedir a circulação de pessoas sobre a estrutura comprometida.

“Aqui tem que ser tomada uma medida imediata, que é a interdição desse ponto. Não permitir o tráfego de pessoas por esse local, principalmente por sobre essa laje, porque a laje já se encontra em estado de comprometimento avançado da sua estabilidade”, afirmou Cleitmã.

Ele explicou que o isolamento deve permanecer até que sejam feitos os reparos necessários para garantir a segurança de quem passa pelo trecho.

Cratera em galeria exposta oferece risco de queda em Teresina; CREA recomenda isolamento imediato — Foto: TV Clube

Moradores afirmam que o problema se agravou com o tempo e a falta de manutenção. A cabeleireira Andréa Lima contou à TV Clube que precisa passar pelo local com frequência e enfrenta dificuldades por causa do fluxo de veículos e da passagem estreita.

“Várias vezes precisei passar e senti muita dificuldade por conta do fluxo de carros e também por ser uma passagem muito estreita. A gente não tem como ter um passeio de pedestre porque exatamente tem essa abertura nesse buraco”, relatou.

Ela também reclamou do mau cheiro e da falta de iluminação no local durante a noite.

“Além do medo e dificuldade, o odor é muito forte, principalmente à noite, que é escuro. Então, assim, é muito perigoso, a gente se sente muito inseguro”, disse.

articles.title: Vazamento de gás provoca princípio de incêndio em pizzaria  | G1
articles.standfirst: Segundo o Corpo de Bombeiros, o homem estava manuseando o fogão quando houve um vazamento de gás, que provocou o princípio de incêndio. Ele sofreu queimaduras nos braços e foi socorrido por terceiros.
articles.summary: Segundo o Corpo de Bombeiros, o homem estava manuseando o fogão quando houve um vazamento de gás, que provocou o princípio de incêndio.
articles.body:
Princípio de incêndio atingiu pizzaria — Foto: Montagem/g1

Um comerciante ficou ferido durante um princípio de incêndio em uma pizzaria em Buenópolis , nesta quarta-feira (16).

Segundo o Corpo de Bombeiros, o homem estava manuseando o fogão quando houve um vazamento de gás, que provocou o princípio de incêndio. Ele sofreu queimaduras nos braços e foi socorrido por terceiros, sendo levado para o hospital da cidade antes da chegada dos militares.

Ainda de acordo com os bombeiros, uma testemunha agiu rapidamente e conseguiu conter o fogo com um extintor. As chamas danificaram um armário de cozinha, um forno de assar pizza e parte da madeira do telhado. A estrutura do comércio não foi comprometida.

Quando os bombeiros chegaram ao local, havia um forte odor de gás. Os militares melhoraram a ventilação natural do ambiente, e o botijão, que já estava vazio, foi colocado na área externa para eliminar os riscos.

articles.title: US drone firm linked to Trump's sons signs MoU with Pakistan Army, secures initial deal
articles.summary: International News: US drone maker Powerus has signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU) with the Pakistan Army that includes an initial order for drones, the company's .
articles.body: US drone maker Powerus has signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU) with the Pakistan Army that includes an initial order for drones, the company's co-founder Brett Velicovich told news agency Reuters on Wednesday.The agreement, which has not been previously reported, comes as Washington and Islamabad work to strengthen their defence and economic relationship. It also brings a Trump family-linked business into focus, as Powerus prepares to merge with a publicly traded company backed by US President Donald Trump's sons.Velicovich said the order involved unmanned aerial systems but declined to disclose the number of drones, their value or other details, citing security sensitivities and confidentiality.Pakistan Army discusses defence cooperation Pakistan's military said a delegation from Powerus, led by Velicovich, met field marshal Asim Munir on Wednesday. The meeting covered defence procurement, production and long-term capacity building.The military's statement did not mention the memorandum or the initial order. Its media wing did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment on the agreement outside business hours.Powerus produces aerial and maritime drones for military and industrial applications. The company is expected to merge with Aureus Greenway Holdings, a publicly traded firm backed by Donald Trump Jr and Eric Trump. Both companies have said they expect the deal to close in early October.Trump sons' investment According to US regulatory filings, the Trump brothers own a stake in Aureus through an investment fund called American Ventures. The fund is expected to hold a 9.9% beneficial ownership stake in the combined company after the merger.Powerus founder and chief executive Andrew Fox said Pakistan's private defence industry is still developing, creating opportunities for US companies to establish a presence in the country."Pakistan's private defence sector remains "emerging but still not mature,"" Fox said, adding that the situation leaves room for US firms to move faster.Velicovich said the company was exploring ways to manufacture technology in Pakistan and build a joint technology relationship between the two countries."The goal would be a joint technology relationship, pairing best-in-breed technology from the U.S. with best-in-breed technology from Pakistan," Velicovich said.Company denies Trump family influence Fox rejected suggestions that Powerus's business growth was connected to the Trump family's involvement in Aureus. He said contracts were awarded on merit and that the Trump sons had "no involvement on the business side" of the company.A spokesman for Donald Trump Jr said he was a passive investor with an indirect holding in the business."Don has no involvement whatsoever in the management or operations of Powerus and plays absolutely no role in the procurement of contracts in the United States or abroad," the spokesperson said."He had no prior knowledge of this deal and had no involvement of any kind in its negotiation, procurement or execution."Eric Trump could not immediately be reached for comment.White House special assistant to the President and principal deputy press secretary Anna Kelly said, "There are no conflicts of interest."The agreement is being announced as relations between Washington and Islamabad improve after years of tensions. Trump has publicly praised Pakistan army chief Munir, while Pakistan has pursued new economic, financial and defence initiatives to strengthen ties with the United States.

articles.title: In 2015, a Florida family followed a metal-detector signal beneath shallow sand and found 51 gold coins and a 40-foot gold chain from a 1715 wreck, worth over $1 million
articles.summary: US News: Another piece of a 300-year-old Spanish treasure story in 2015 was recovered off the Florida coast, when the Schmitt family recovered 51 gold coins an.
articles.body: Another piece of a 300-year-old Spanish treasure story in 2015 was recovered off the Florida coast, when the Schmitt family recovered 51 gold coins and about 40 feet of ornate gold chain from the wreck of the flagship of Spain’s 1715 treasure fleet, Capitana. The haul was valued at more than $1 million and included a rare 1715 Royal Mexico Eight Escudos coin known as the “Tricentennial Royal.” TIME reported that the Schmitt family, who were professional treasure hunters working as subcontractors for 1715 Fleet-Queens Jewels LLC, had discovered the treasure off Florida’s coast.A fleet caught in a hurricaneThe Capitana was part of a Spanish fleet that was carrying gold, silver, and other valuable cargo from the Americas toward Spain. On July 30 and 31, 1715, the ships were caught in a hurricane while sailing past the Florida coast. National Geographic reported that 11 of the fleet’s 12 ships were lost during the storm, and scattered their cargo along the coastline. The wrecks subsequently became targets for generations of salvors and treasure hunters. The Capitana was among the vessels searched repeatedly, and modern recovery operations eventually brought individual coins and other artifacts back to the surface.The Schmitt family had already been involved in searching the 1715 wrecks for years, and TIME reported that the family had first found gold in 2013. Their later discovery from the Capitana became one of the more notable recoveries from the wreck because of both the number of gold coins and the unusual piece of jewelry found with them.The coin that stood outThe centerpiece of the recovery was a Royal Mexico Eight Escudos dated 1715, a coin that was struck during the same year the fleet was lost. It became known as the “Tricentennial Royal” because its recovery came roughly 300 years after it was made and lost at sea. TIME reported that the rare coin alone was valued at more than $500,000. The rest of the haul included dozens of other gold coins and a long, ornate gold chain.The Numismatic Guaranty Company documented the 2015 recovery and gives the date as June 18, 2015. It records the find as 51 gold coins and 40 feet of ornate gold chain, with the Tricentennial Royal identified as the centerpiece. Most of the recovered coins were minted in Lima, Peru, and included eight- and two-escudo denominations, which also illustrates why shipwreck coins can be valuable beyond their gold content.A discovery timed to historyThe recovery was made public in July 2015, rather than immediately after the find. National Geographic reported that the discovery had been made in June and that the Schmitt family waited to announce it so the news would coincide with the 300th anniversary of the fleet’s sinking. The divers were working in about 15 feet of water roughly 1,000 feet from a beach near Fort Pierce, Florida. Three centuries earlier, the hurricane had scattered the fleet and its cargo along the Florida coast, and in 2015, the anniversary brought attention back to the same wreck site as divers recovered objects that had remained buried beneath the seabed for generations.The NGC record shows that the Capitana produced another major recovery later that summer, when 350 gold coins were recovered on July 30 and 31, exactly 300 years after the fleet’s destruction. For the Schmitt family, however, the earlier June recovery remained particularly notable since the combination of 51 gold coins, a 40-foot chain, and a rare 1715 Royal turned a section of Florida’s seabed into a time capsule from one of Spain’s most famous treasure fleets.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: ISIS-inspired shooting suspect identified as former Reddit moderator
articles.summary: US News: A man accused of preparing an ISIS-inspired mass shooting was identified in a social-media post as a former moderator of r/doordash, Reddit’s communit.
articles.body: A man accused of preparing an ISIS-inspired mass shooting was identified in a social-media post as a former moderator of r/doordash, Reddit’s community for the food-delivery platform DoorDash. The account operated under the username “u/i_love_femboys6969”. Federal records identify its user as Jonathan Hunter Kramer, 21, of Valencia, Pennsylvania.Investigators tied the account to Kramer through login credentials recovered from his laptop and Reddit subscriber records associated with his email address and phone number.Polymarket highlighted the r/doordash moderator connection. The federal affidavit does not itself identify r/doordash, though it records “u/i_love_femboys6969” saying it was “open to moderating any subreddit”.How did the FBI track Kramer before his arrest?The Reddit activity formed one part of a broader federal investigation that culminated in Kramer’s arrest in September.Kramer faces a federal firearms charge over allegations that he received a gun and ammunition knowing, or having reason to believe, they would be used in a felony or terrorism offence. Prosecutors say the alleged terrorism conduct involved providing, attempting to provide or conspiring to provide material support to ISIS.Agents tracking Kramer on September 12 followed him from his home to a Walmart, where he bought a disposable phone. He later met another person outside the store and took possession of an elongated black bag from that person’s vehicle; an FBI agent believed it was large enough to contain a rifle.Kramer then travelled to a hotel in Cranberry Township and booked a week-long stay with cash. He later visited a sporting-goods shop before returning to the hotel, where agents approached him.The searches that followed uncovered about 190 rounds of rifle ammunition, a semiautomatic rifle and five magazines, along with a scope, bipod and pepper spray, investigators said. About 30 knives were recovered separately from Kramer’s residence. Federal agents arrested him after the searches.‘Preparing for my mission’: What investigators found onlineInvestigators were also examining another strand of Kramer’s alleged online activity — a SimpleX user calling himself “Hamza Al Rashid”. The FBI linked the persona to Kramer after comparing the account’s activity with other information gathered during the investigation.On September 9, three days before Kramer’s arrest, “Hamza Al Rashid” wrote that he was “preparing for my mission” and indicated that obtaining a weapon was the remaining step before he would be ready.The account had also allegedly discussed an attack on a crowd with an FBI confidential human source, including the possible use of smoke and pepper grenades. Investigators separately found that Kramer had previously purchased pepper spray online.Authorities further allege that “Hamza Al Rashid” expressed support for ISIS and communicated with others about attacks and violent material. The persona was also linked to a SimpleX group called “The Brotherhood”, which investigators say was run by “Hamza Al Rashid”.FBI traces more Reddit activity to KramerThe investigation into Kramer’s online footprint extended beyond the “Hamza Al Rashid” persona.Investigators identified “u/slopdestroyer” as an alternate Reddit account after “u/i_love_femboys6969” referred to it that way. Posts associated with the second account included material showing ISIS fighters or supporters and an ISIS nasheed.Agents also found overlap between the Reddit activity and the SimpleX account. In July, “u/i_love_femboys6969” recommended the encrypted messaging service SimpleX, while “Hamza Al Rashid” separately promoted the same platform as a secure means of communication.What happened in Kramer’s earlier juvenile case?The September investigation was not Kramer’s first contact with law enforcement.He had come to authorities’ attention as a juvenile in 2023 over an alleged mass-casualty plot. The Justice Department says he was later adjudicated delinquent for his role in that case and for possession of child sexual abuse material. During the same investigation, an FBI agent said a recording recovered from Kramer’s laptop depicted what the agent described as a pledge of allegiance to ISIS leader Abu Bakr al-Baghdadi.After Kramer was released from a Pennsylvania juvenile facility in March 2026, the FBI received another tip raising concerns about his online behaviour and renewed contact with people he had known before the earlier case. That tip helped set in motion the investigation that eventually led agents back to his online accounts and, months later, to his arrest.The current case remains at the criminal-complaint stage and the accusations have not been adjudicated. Kramer retains the presumption of innocence. He appeared in federal court on September 14. Prosecutors are seeking to keep him in custody while the case proceeds, citing what they describe as a threat to public safety.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: In 1978, two boys digging in a Los Angeles yard found a buried Ferrari; Farmers Insurance recovered the three-year-hidden Dino and sold it through a special sealed-bid auction
articles.summary: US News: In 1978, two boys digging in a Los Angeles backyard unearthed a stolen Ferrari that had been missing for over three years, leading to an extraordinary recovery story involving Farmers Insurance and a rare collector's auction.
articles.body: Ordinary digging in a Los Angeles backyard in 1978 led to the discovery of a Ferrari that had been missing for more than three years. According to the Los Angeles Times, two boys playing in the backyard of a house on West 119th Street in Los Angeles were digging in the mud in February 1978 when they found something unusual just below the surface. They told sheriff’s deputies that it felt like the roof of a car. Investigators returned with a skid-steer loader and shovels and uncovered a green 1974 Ferrari, which had been reported stolen in December 1974. The car was found in good condition despite having been buried underground for more than three years.The Ferrari disappeared in 1974Rosendo Cruz of Alhambra bought the Dino in October 1974. Just two months later, on December 7, Cruz reported the Ferrari stolen, and Farmers Insurance reimbursed him for the loss. The theft report remained on file with the Los Angeles Police Department, but the car was missing from the record for more than three years.When the car was excavated, the discovery suggested that the vehicle had been deliberately buried, not abandoned. The Ferrari was thought to have been covered with rugs and other materials, even though some portions of the car remained uncovered in the moist soil. Although Southern California's relatively dry climate may have helped preserve some of the car, it still required restoration after spending years underground.The car was particularly significant because it was not just any Ferrari, but a Dino 246, a model known for its distinctive design and engineering. According to Motor Sport Magazine, the Ferrari Dino 246 GT was styled by Pininfarina and powered by a 2.4-litre, 65-degree V6 mounted transversely ahead of the rear wheels. The fixed-roof GT was followed in 1972 by the 246 GTS, a targa-style version with a detachable roof panel. The GTS retained the GT's basic mechanical layout while adding an open-air design.From buried car to insurance auctionAfter the Ferrari was recovered, Farmers Insurance faced an unusual question: what should it do with a car that had already been paid out as a theft claim? Since the company had reimbursed the original owner, the recovered vehicle became its property. Rather than simply sell it through an ordinary used-car transaction, Farmers arranged a special sealed-bid auction. By then, the case was already well known, and potential buyers were eager to see the Ferrari. The auction process produced another twist. The car was shown to prospective buyers, but some parts appeared to go missing during the exhibition period. Farmers realised that many of the initial bids were not genuine. The eventual sale turned the buried Dino from an insurance recovery into a collector’s car with an extraordinary history. Its unusual past was now part of its appeal, alongside the Ferrari name and the rarity of the 246 GTS.The Dino returns to the roadIt was not long until the car had gone through numerous owners and fell into the possession of Ferrari fanatic Brad Howard. After some time, the vehicle was restored. The work included mechanical repairs and cosmetic restoration. Giuseppe Cappalonga, who was an expert on Ferraris, worked on restoring the vehicle. The restoration appears to have preserved the Ferrari’s unusual history. It went from being reported stolen in 1974 to being recovered in 1978, auctioned by the insurer, and eventually restored by collectors. The restoration did not wipe away the Dino’s past. Instead, it put the car back on the road while leaving its unusual history intact. From being stolen and buried to being found years later and restored, the Dino had already lived through more than most classic cars ever do. Its survival became part of what made the Ferrari so memorable.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Australia to bar foreign students from bringing families, target 225,000 net migration by 2028
articles.summary: Rest of World News: Australia is preparing to stop international students from bringing their partners and children with them while they study, as the government moves to.
articles.body: Australia is preparing to stop international students from bringing their partners and children with them while they study, as the government moves to reduce migration and tighten rules for temporary visa holders, media reports said on Thursday.Home affairs minister Tony Burke is expected to announce the changes in a speech at the National Press Club later in the day. The government plans to bring net overseas migration down to 225,000 by 2028, compared with about 300,000 currently, public broadcaster ABC News reported. Burke's office did not immediately respond to a request for comment.New restrictions on student familiesUnder the current system, international students can bring dependent children under 18 to Australia. Their spouses or partners are also allowed to work, although the number of hours they can work depends on the student's course.The proposed changes would remove the option for students to bring their families while they study. The government is also expected to tighten rules governing temporary migrants who want to switch to another visa.Migration becomes a political issueThe announcement comes as the hard-right One Nation party gains support in recent polls and pushes for a much larger reduction in temporary migration.The party said this week that it wanted to cut the number of temporary migrants by 750,000 over three years, giving Australians "breathing space".One Nation describes its approach as "Australia first" and has proposed reducing net overseas migration to 130,000 after the initial three-year period. It says the programme would be reviewed every year.Student numbers and pressure on housingAustralia's migration intake rose sharply after the country reopened its borders in February 2022, following nearly two years of Covid restrictions. International students, backpackers and temporary skilled workers contributed to the increase.Migration has since declined over the past two years, but critics continue to argue that high numbers of newcomers are putting pressure on housing and infrastructure and affecting social cohesion.Official figures show net overseas migration reached 306,000 in the year to June 30, 2025. International students accounted for more than half of that total. Net migration stood at 429,000 in 2024, after reaching a record 518,000 in 2023.The proposed restrictions would affect international students and other temporary migrants, as the government seeks to reduce the overall number of people entering and remaining in Australia.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: In 2017, a Mauritanian meteorite hunter found a 12-pound piece of the Moon; the “Moon Puzzle” was later sold at auction for $612,500
articles.summary: Rest of World News: In 2017, a rare lunar meteorite known as 'NWA 11789' was discovered in Mauritania and later sold at auction for $612,500, showcasing its incredible journey from the Moon to Earth.
articles.body: A meteorite was found in Mauritania in 2017, and was classified as Northwest Africa 11789, and was a lunar meteorite that consisted of fragments that could be fitted together to form a mass weighing about 5.5 kilograms, or slightly more than 12 pounds. In 2018, the unusual specimen went to auction and sold for $612,500.A meteorite from the MoonThe specimen was officially classified as a lunar feldspathic breccia, which means it is a rock made from broken and reassembled fragments of lunar material. The Meteoritical Bulletin database records NWA 11789 as an official meteorite, with 2017 being the year it was found, Mauritania as its country of origin and a recorded mass of 5.49 kilograms. The database also says the material was purchased in Mauritania by meteorite collector Dustin Dickens from an anonymous meteorite hunter.The specimen’s pieces could be fitted back together, which produced the distinctive appearance that eventually gave it the nickname “The Moon Puzzle.” Lunar meteorites are pieces of the Moon that reached Earth naturally, and these rocks arrived without being deliberately brought back by astronauts, unlike the lunar samples collected during the Apollo missions.Six fragments that fit togetherGeekWire reported that the meteorite consisted of six fragments that fitted together like pieces of a jigsaw puzzle, and created a mass of about 5.5 kilograms, or 12 pounds. The auction description from RR Auction similarly identified NWA 11789 as a lunar feldspathic breccia and described six pieces fitting together to form a mass slightly above 12 pounds. The rock also carried a partial fusion crust, which is a feature produced by heating as a meteorite travels through Earth's atmosphere. The surface had been exposed to the intense heating that is generally associated with atmospheric entry, while the interior preserved fragments of lunar rock.The official Meteoritical Bulletin classification also recorded the specimen as a feldspathic breccia and placed its total mass at 5.49 kilograms. It identified the main mass as being held by Dustin Dickens, with a type specimen deposited at the University of New Mexico.A $612,500 auction saleThe Moon Puzzle moved from scientific curiosity to high-value collectible in October 2018, when Boston-based RR Auction offered the specimen for sale, and the winning bid reached $612,500. GeekWire reported that the successful bidder was a representative working with the Tam Chuc Pagoda Complex in Vietnam, and the complex planned to display the meteorite, which gave the lunar material a public-facing destination after its sale.RR Auction lists the specimen as having sold for $615,000 including the buyer’s premium. The reported winning bid itself was $612,500, which is the figure widely reported at the time. Lunar meteorites are rare scientific specimens, and NWA 11789 offered several unusual characteristics at once, such as its confirmed lunar origin, its large mass, its multiple matching fragments and its visible fusion crust.The material originated on the Moon, was blasted from the lunar surface by an impact in the distant past, traveled through space and eventually reached Earth. Years later, fragments found in the Mauritanian desert were reassembled into a specimen that collectors could recognize as a piece of another world.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: 'It can't be that Hindi will not be taught in Tamil Nadu', SC tells state during hearing on Navodaya schools
articles.summary: India News: NEW DELHI: Supreme Court on Thursday directed the Tamil Nadu government to comply with its December 15, 2025 order to identify land in every district .
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Supreme Court on Thursday directed the Tamil Nadu government to comply with its December 15, 2025 order to identify land in every district for establishing Jawahar Navodaya Vidyalayas, while urging the state and Centre to resolve their differences over the schools through dialogue.A bench of Justices BV Nagarathna and Augustine George Masih also questioned Tamil Nadu's opposition to the three-language policy followed by Navodaya schools and said the state should not view the establishment of the centrally funded institutions as a threat to its existing education system."You have to change your mindset, it can’t be that Hindi will not be taught in the soil of Tamil Nadu," Justice Nagarathna observed during the hearing.The bench also said the people in Chennai should not alienate those in Delhi while stressing the need for cooperative federalism."We are saying in addition to all the good things you’re doing in your State, having something in addition will not bring down your standards. Coming from Delhi, will not lower the standards of Chennai. People in Chennai should not alienate Delhi and vice versa," the Court said.The court granted Tamil Nadu three more months to identify suitable land in each district and directed representatives of the state and Central governments to hold further discussions on the policy for establishing the schools. The matter has been posted for December 14.Tamil Nadu raises language concernsThe case relates to Tamil Nadu's challenge to a Madras High Court direction to establish Navodaya Vidyalayas in every district.Navodaya schools are centrally funded, co-educational residential schools run by the Navodaya Vidyalaya Samiti under the Union Ministry of Education. Tamil Nadu has opposed their establishment, among other reasons, because the schools follow a three-language policy that includes Hindi, while the state follows a two-language policy.Senior Advocate Jaideep Gupta, appearing for Tamil Nadu, told the court that the state's objection was not to schools or the teaching of Hindi as such, but to the language policy associated with the Navodaya scheme."It is against the State policy. It supersedes Tamil. This kind of unification is not the purport of the Constitution. It is not a Central government school. It is a school run by a society. There is an adamancy that Hindi must predominate."Justice Nagarathna said the language issue could be discussed between the Centre and the state."If you want Tamil as a second language, it is a matter which can be considered," the Judge said, asking the state Secretary to speak to the corresponding Central government Secretary.Gupta said discussions had already taken place but the Centre had remained adamant about Hindi. He nevertheless agreed to another round of consultations.Court stresses cooperative federalismTamil Nadu also argued that the judiciary could not compel a state to adopt an optional Central government policy through a mandamus.Gupta submitted that education is in the Concurrent List and that Tamil Nadu has constitutional authority to frame its own education policy. He also argued that the Navodaya scheme was not compulsory.Justice Nagarathna questioned the consequences of individual states refusing to accept Central policies."Education is in the Concurrent List. There has to be cooperative federalism. If each State says that I don't accept your policy, what will happen?" the Judge asked.The bench said Tamil Nadu could continue running its own institutions and following its own syllabus, while Navodaya schools would provide an additional educational option.The court also rejected the argument that the establishment of Navodaya schools would lower Tamil Nadu's educational standards."We are not alienating you and we are not alienating them. Some more type of schools come in your state also which will only enhance the high standard which we are aware of. This is not going to lower your standards. If Navodaya schools were going to lower the standard of education in Tamil Nadu we would have said that irrespective of what you would have said. That is not the case here. It will provide more opportunity," Justice Nagarathna told Gupta."Ultimately everybody must work together," Justice Nagarathna said.State raises financial concernsTamil Nadu also raised financial concerns, submitting that the Centre had promised to release Rs 5,000 crore for education but had not done so.Gupta argued that the state could not take on additional financial liabilities when funds under existing schemes had allegedly not been released.Additional Solicitor General KM Nataraj, appearing for the Centre, submitted that the state's primary requirement under the scheme was to provide land, while construction and other expenses would be borne by the Central government.Nataraj said the scheme was at an early stage and construction would take several years, during which the language-related differences could be addressed through discussions.Gupta, however, said around 30 acres of land would be required in each district and that identifying land before deciding whether to accept the policy would create difficulties.The bench clarified that it was not directing the state to acquire land immediately, but only to identify suitable land in its government plan.Supreme Court refuses to recall land directionThe Supreme Court had in December 2025 directed Tamil Nadu to identify land required for establishing Navodaya Vidyalayas in every district within six weeks. The state subsequently sought recall of the order.On Thursday, the bench declined to recall the direction and instead granted the state three months to comply.In its order, the bench recorded that Tamil Nadu had cited the change in government and lack of material progress in discussions with the Centre as reasons for non-compliance."Be that as it may, we direct the petitioner to comply with our order of 15.12.2025 in so far as identification of the land necessary to establish the school in each district," the order stated.The bench also directed the Centre and Tamil Nadu to continue discussions on the policy while the state works on identifying the land.Advocates G Priyadarshini and Rahul Shyam Bhandari, appearing for Kumari Maha Sabha, the petitioner before the High Court, argued that Tamil Nadu could not deny students access to free education through Navodaya schools."The Court should not get into this debate," Gupta said during the hearing.Justice Nagarathna responded: "That perception that you are surrendering to the central govt should not be there."Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: In 1997, an Illinois fisherman began pulling Mississippi River trash alone; his cleanup grew into nearly 140,000 volunteers who removed 14.2 million pounds
articles.summary: US News: Discover how Chad Pregracke turned his passion for a cleaner Mississippi River into a massive volunteer movement, removing over 14 million pounds of trash with 140,000 volunteers. Learn about his inspiring journey and the impact of Living Lands and Waters in restoring America’s rivers.
articles.body: The majority of individuals who are angry about pollution either file a petition, send a letter, or just complain to anyone who will listen. Few believe that getting a boat and beginning to remove the trash yourself is the only practical approach. Even fewer transform that one choice into a movement with tens of thousands of volunteers and dozens of rivers. That is essentially the trajectory of Chad Pregracke's career, which started off as a simple annoyance at what he kept seeing beneath the surface of the river he grew up next to rather than with a big strategy.Pregracke was raised in East Moline, Illinois, with the Mississippi River essentially as his backyard. As a youngster working as a commercial shell diver for the cultivated pearl industry, he spent extended periods underwater, becoming more and more shocked at what he found there: thousands of tyres, discarded barrels, abandoned automobiles and even the tops of school buses littering the riverbed. As a teenager, he began by writing to government officials and asking them to do something about it.Deciding to do it himselfIn 1997, at 22, Pregracke landed a tiny grant from the aluminium firm Alcoa and decided that if no one else was going to clean the river, he would. He spent that year alone, mostly from an old boat, removing more than 45,000 pounds of trash from a stretch of the Mississippi, pulling the debris out one piece at a time and, in the early days, dumping a lot of it on his parents’ front lawn, an arrangement that didn’t last long once the neighbours noticed.Local media caught up on the oddity of one young man taking a position that appeared to be a government agency’s, and suddenly the attention snowballed. A year later, in 1998, Pregracke codified his efforts by forming a nonprofit organisation, Living Lands and Waters, which gave the initiative the structure and fundraising ability it needed to develop beyond one guy and one boat.From one boat to a professional cleanup crewWhat began as Pregracke’s solo effort eventually became a staffed operation with barges, workboats and heavy equipment. Living Lands and Waters says its crews can spend up to nine months a year travelling between rivers for cleanups, restoration projects and environmental education.Over the decades, crews have hauled out far more than regular debris from America’s waterways. Pregracke’s crews have hauled out washing machines, tractors, pianos and refrigerators, along with the plastic bottles and food wrappers more commonly associated with river litter. Some of the larger objects were deliberately discarded, while others entered the river through accidents, flooding or years of neglect. Each of those objects presented its own silent hazard, seeping oil, refrigerant or other pollutants into a river system that provides drinking water for millions of people in dozens of American towns.The statistics, decades onBy 2025, the totals had ballooned into numbers that would have looked incredible to the 22-year-old working alone on a tiny grant nearly three decades earlier. The National Mississippi River Museum and Aquarium, which awarded Pregracke for his achievement in protecting the river, says his efforts have inspired thousands of volunteers in river communities who would never have been directly involved with the waterway that runs through their towns. Today, Living Lands and Waters has around 140,000 volunteers who have taken part in cleanups, removing more than 14 million pounds of debris from 33 rivers in 23 states.This initiative has earned recognition far beyond the river villages themselves. The crew of Pregracke now has a fleet that includes barges, towboats, workboats, skid steers and heavy equipment that can pull out debris no ordinary volunteer group could handle alone, a far cry from the single small boat he started with, according to Points of Light, the volunteer service organisation that has followed his progress over the years. Since then the charity has grown well beyond simple cleanups, including a tree planting initiative that has planted more than a million seedlings back along riverbanks and educational activities that bring students onto the water for hands-on learning about the ecosystem they live beside.What started as a teen’s frustration over an ignored problem has, nearly thirty years later, become one of the longest-running grassroots environmental efforts in American history, proof that sometimes the easiest way to deal with a problem nobody else will solve is to just start fixing it yourself, one piece of trash at a time.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: EU moves to ban social media for under-13s, tighten rules for teenagers
articles.summary: Europe News: The European Commission has proposed banning children under 13 from using social media across the European Union and restricting access for older teen.
articles.body: The European Commission has proposed banning children under 13 from using social media across the European Union and restricting access for older teenagers under a new EU Kids Act, European Commission president Ursula von der Leyen announced on Thursday."Today, our children are engaging with some of the most sophisticated technology ever created, and it was not created with children's well-being and development in mind," von der Leyen told a press conference.Earlier on Wednesday, Von der Leyen had said the Commission would adopt a “gradual and differentiated approach”, with different safeguards based on age.“No social media under the age of 13. No personal account under the age of 15,” she told the European Parliament in Strasbourg on Wednesday.Under the proposed framework, children aged 13 to under 15 would be allowed only “mini accounts” set up and supervised by parents or guardians, with limited features and a one-hour-a-day time restriction. For those aged 15 to 18, platforms would be required to implement “safe design”.Social media, video-sharing platforms, online games, AI companions and chatbots serving under-18s would face new safeguards, Reuters reported on Thursday. These would prohibit addictive features, profiling-based recommendation feeds, infinite scrolling, reward mechanisms and unsolicited contact from strangers. AI companions and chatbots would be disabled by default, while platforms would need child-safe algorithms and accessible parental controls.“I am aware that many perceive the power of big tech as overwhelming and impossible to roll back. I disagree,” von der Leyen said.“We do not have to accept addictive features. We do not have to accept children being drawn into ever more extreme content. We do not have to accept that girls have their photos used for AI-generated sexualised images,” she said.Von der Leyen said the proposal would also shift responsibility towards technology companies.“So we are reversing the burden of proof. Platforms will have to prove that they are safe,” she said. “Because it is not about our minors accessing social media. It is about when and how do we allow social media to access minors.”“Europe has the power to act. It is we who decide our rules, not big tech,” she added.The Commission’s proposal follows regulatory efforts in Australia, Britain, China, India, Turkey and several European countries. AP reported that platforms including Facebook, Instagram and TikTok already prohibit users under 13 from opening accounts, but authorities have accused companies of failing to keep children off their services.The proposal still has to be negotiated with EU member states and the European Parliament before it can become law. The Commission is also preparing a broader Digital Fairness Act, with von der Leyen saying, “Addictive design, for example, is harming everyone. This is why we need a wider framework, the Digital Fairness Act. We will propose it in autumn.”Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: A 70-year-old hiker disappeared on Michigan's remote Isle Royale for a week; backpackers helped find him injured and hypothermic before a Coast Guard helicopter hoisted him out
articles.summary: US News: A 70-year-old hiker who disappeared during a solo trip to Michigan’s remote Isle Royale National Park has been found alive after more than a week, end.
articles.body: A 70-year-old hiker who disappeared during a solo trip to Michigan’s remote Isle Royale National Park has been found alive after more than a week, ending a search that involved police, search dogs, aircraft and fellow backpackers. According to the U.S. Coast Guard, Craig Berg was located injured and suffering from hypothermia on September 12 before being airlifted from the Lake Superior island for medical treatment. The rescue was also reported by MPR News and CBS Detroit. His safe recovery brought relief after days of uncertainty as crews searched the rugged island wilderness.Search began after Berg failed to returnBerg, from Royal Oak, Michigan, had been on a solo hiking trip through Isle Royale. He was expected to return on September 5 but did not make his scheduled ferry, prompting his family to report him missing the following day. Search operations continued for days as authorities tried to locate him across the rugged wilderness of the national park. Isle Royale is a remote island in Lake Superior, stretching about 45 miles long and nine miles wide. The park has an extensive network of rugged hiking trails but no roads or motor vehicles across most of the island, making a search particularly challenging.Backpackers played a crucial role in finding himThe breakthrough came when fellow backpackers located Berg and alerted authorities. Michigan State Police troopers and K-9 teams were involved in the search, working alongside the National Park Service and other agencies. The search effort also involved personnel and resources from the Michigan Department of Natural Resources, the U.S. Coast Guard, Wisconsin and Minnesota authorities, and No One Left Behind K9 Search & Rescue. Berg was found injured and hypothermic but conscious and alert. The circumstances that led to him becoming stranded, as well as the precise location where he was found, have not been fully disclosed by authorities.Coast Guard helicopter airlifts him from Isle RoyaleAfter Berg was located, a U.S. Coast Guard MH-60 Jayhawk helicopter from Air Station Traverse City flew to the island. The crew hoisted him aboard and transported him to Marquette Regional Airport in Gwinn, Michigan. Emergency medical personnel were waiting at the airport and took Berg to a local hospital for further treatment. Authorities have not released additional details about the extent of his injuries or his current medical condition. The airlift followed a coordinated response that had been underway for several days.Michigan State Police troopers and K-9 teams had been deployed to the island to assist with the search. Coast Guard crews also transported personnel and equipment to Isle Royale as the operation expanded. The remote terrain and island’s wilderness setting made locating Berg particularly challenging for search teams.The successful rescue brought an end to a complex, multi-agency search in one of the Midwest’s most isolated wilderness areas. Officials credited the combined efforts of professional rescuers, law enforcement agencies and members of the public, particularly the backpackers whose assistance helped lead search teams to Berg.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: In 2014, an Australian family began restoring their 120-acre farm; 12 years later, Bower Estate is a thriving native habitat that hosts weddings
articles.summary: Rest of World News: Remember the scene from the Twilight saga, where Edward and Bella exchange vows in a clearing surrounded by wisteria and candlelight, the whole thing .
articles.body: Remember the scene from the Twilight saga, where Edward and Bella exchange vows in a clearing surrounded by wisteria and candlelight, the whole thing bathed in soft woodland light? Though fantasy, the scene stayed with enough people that forest weddings have become shorthand for intimate, magical, just-us-against-the-world celebrations. What if you could have a similar wedding in the midst of a forest that looks straight out of a fairytale?Getting married in a forest does feel different. There's something about woodland ceremonies: the intimacy, the dappled light and the feeling that you have stepped into a fantasy world. Bower Estate delivers exactly that aesthetic. Trees, suspended greenery and a transparent marquee that disappears into the hinterland sky create the kind of secluded clearing you'd think only existed in fiction. Tucked away in the Queensland hinterland near Natural Bridge, the family estate provides a dream-like wedding venue. You get the clearing and the greenery, and it dissolves into the hinterland sky so the forest becomes the actual backdrop. And your wedding could be making an actual difference. Every celebration on this 120-acre property funds active conservation work. The couple gets their forest vows, and the land gets another season of regeneration.Farmland to conservation projectThe Bower is nestled in the Gold Coast Hinterland, near the New South Wales border in Natural Bridge. The land is surrounded by some of the most beautiful national parks in Queensland. In 2014, the family bought 120 acres of property that was once used for timber logging and dairy farming. Then they started transforming the land. The kind of unglamorous work that rarely gets any attention: bush regeneration, fencing and replanting native species. The family has been caring about nature and animals for more than three decades, which they also taught their children. After buying this farmland, they applied for grants, partnered with local research initiatives and documented species returning as the habitat improved.“Our family wanted this estate to be more than just a place for events and weddings; it’s a long-term conservation project. Your celebrations help the bigger picture of this land and preserve our flora and fauna for generations to come,” the family says on the estate's website.By the early 2020s, they saw noticeable changes. Native species that hadn't inhabited the area in decades began showing up. “In the last few years we have been lucky to see wallaby, platypus and koala species return to the area through these projects,” they said. The family also registered the property with Land for Wildlife, Queensland's voluntary programme for private landholders managing wildlife habitat.Hosting weddings, serving natureThe weddings became the means of funding these conservation projects. A couple's celebration on a summer evening could fund months of conservation work. A custom-built transparent marquee can accommodate up to 140 guests. Couples get unobstructed hinterland views by day and the southern sky at night. No competing structures or distractions, just pure nature.The Bower Cottage, which is the original farmhouse, has been restored into a luxury three-bedroom cottage that can accommodate up to 10 people. The cottage comes with a sprawling verandah, a space for small wedding parties or bridal preparation. It can accommodate about 100 standing guests.Guests can also take eco-tours, which include hikes through the pristine trails in the lush forest, exploring the culinary heritage, garden tours and enjoying outdoor activities. The location itself carries spectacle beyond what a venue brochure typically offers. Two kilometres up the road sits Natural Bridge, a section of Springbrook National Park where a waterfall cascades through a cave by day, and at night, the roof of the cave is illuminated by glowworms. The Bower Estate offers the kind of magic one may only see in fantasy films.Along with preserving the forests and wildlife corridors, the estate also supports local growers and producers. After the wedding, guests take home jars of honey from the Bower Bees. Native raspberries make it to the desserts. They provide a venue for all kinds of events. There is an on-site catering team taking care of the food, as well as event coordination.The estate's calendar now stretches beyond weddings: it offers wellness retreats, lovely lunches, eco-education programmes and paddock-to-plate picnic days. Bookings are already being made years in advance, with 2028 dates currently open for those interested.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: 'Your leadership has transformed India into a world power': Netanyahu greets PM Modi on 76th birthday
articles.summary: India News: Israeli prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Thursday extended birthday greetings to Prime Minister Narendra Modi, describing the India-Israel relatio.
articles.body: Israeli prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Thursday extended birthday greetings to Prime Minister Narendra Modi, describing the India-Israel relationship as an “unprecedented partnership” and saying the friendship between the two countries had “never been stronger”.Birthday greetings poured in from across the world, with foreign leaders, envoys and diplomatic missions highlighting India’s bilateral partnerships and Modi’s role in strengthening ties. Russian president Vladimir Putin praised his contribution to the “special and privileged strategic partnership” between India and Russia, while Italian prime minister Giorgia Meloni wished Modi “health, energy, and success”.“Happy birthday, Narendra!” Netanyahu wrote in a post on X, alongside an image of the two leaders. “Your leadership has transformed India into a world power. Together, we have built an unprecedented partnership between our two great democracies.”The Modi-Netanyahu bonhomie has become a prominent feature of India-Israel ties, with both leaders repeatedly highlighting their personal friendship and political trust. Their meetings and public exchanges have highlighted a relationship that extends beyond formal diplomacy into close strategic cooperation.“The friendship between Israel and India has never been stronger, and together we will take it to even greater heights,” he added, wishing Modi “many more years of leadership, health and fulfillment”.India and Israel established full diplomatic relations in 1992, while PM Modi’s July 2017 visit to Israel elevated the relationship to a strategic partnership. Netanyahu followed with a visit to India in January 2018.The relationship now covers defence, security, technology, agriculture, water, innovation, trade and other areas. During PM Modi’s visit to Israel in February 2026, Netanyahu described him as “my dear friend” and said, “You are more than a friend; you are a brother in many respects.” He also said, “Israel is stronger than ever and India is stronger than ever.”Netanyahu's birthday message came days after India hosted the 18th BRICS Summit in New Delhi, where the grouping adopted a New Delhi Declaration that included strong references to the Israel-Lebanon conflict and the Gaza war.On Lebanon, BRICS leaders said, “We welcome the ceasefire in Lebanon” and called for full implementation of UN Security Council Resolution 1701. The declaration also called on Israel to “withdraw its occupying forces from all of the Lebanese territories, in which they remain”.That diplomatic contrast has not, so far, translated into a visible rupture in India-Israel ties. Netanyahu’s latest message instead points to continued political engagement, while New Delhi maintains separate tracks with Israel, Arab countries and the wider BRICS grouping.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.summary: MUMBAI: Shiv Sena (UBT) president Uddhav Thackeray on Thursday said he would initiate legal action if the “character assassination” campaign targeting.
articles.body: MUMBAI: Shiv Sena (UBT) president Uddhav Thackeray on Thursday said he would initiate legal action if the “character assassination” campaign targeting his family over the 2020 Disha Salian death case did not stop.The former Maharashtra chief minister spoke on the issue days after the Bombay high court ordered a CBI probe into Salian’s death following a petition filed by her father.The central agency subsequently registered a case without naming any accused, news agency PTI reported.“We have no connection with this case. Aaditya (Thackeray) has also said so. This issue is not merely about me. Such character assassination can take place with you people too,” Thackeray said.“If such allegations are made continuously, how long one should tolerate it? I am wondering why the names of Modi and Trump are absent in this case,” he said sarcastically.Thackeray reiterated that Salian’s death was an unfortunate incident and that his family had no connection with it, PTI reported.“It is politically motivated. We were quiet because an SIT was probing the case. Those who want to investigate, they can keep investigating. But enough of this pointless character assassination, or else we will initiate legal steps,” the Sena (UBT) chief said.Sanjay Raut backs AadityaMeanwhile, Shiv Sena (UBT) leader Sanjay Raut on Thursday backed Aaditya Thackeray and said “people trust the Thackeray family”.The CBI registered an FIR in the 2020 Disha Salian death case, naming no accused, in compliance with Bombay high court directives on a petition filed by her father.Aaditya had claimed on Wednesday that some people were deliberately trying to link his name to the case to tarnish his character for political reasons.Raut said the CBI FIR was an attempt to malign the image of the Thackeray family.“We are ready to fight. He (Aaditya) is not alone in this,” Raut said while responding to questions about Aaditya’s claim that he never knew or met Salian, PTI reported.“People trust the Thackeray family,” Raut added.Raut also hit out at the Rane family, arch-rivals of the Thackerays, and said they should present any evidence related to Salian’s death to the CBI.The Ranes have alleged a link between the Thackerays and the case.Aaditya denies knowing SalianOn Wednesday, Aaditya Thackeray had claimed that he had never met Disha Salian.“I have never met or known Disha Salian. Linking my name to this tragic case is a deliberate, evidence-free attempt of character assassination by a few individuals with clear political and personal motives, for almost six years,” Aaditya said in a post on X.Salian, 28, a former manager of Bollywood actor Sushant Singh Rajput, died on June 8, 2020, after falling from the 12th floor of a residential building in Mumbai’s Malad area.Police had claimed that it was a case of suicide.A week later, Rajput was found dead in his Bandra apartment on June 14, 2020, triggering speculation about a possible link between the two deaths.On September 2, the Bombay high court ordered a CBI probe into Salian’s death while pulling up the Mumbai Police for failing to register an FIR for six years and observing that its investigation raised more questions than answers.(With agency inputs)You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Mumbai | Silver Rate in Mumbai | Bank Holidays in Mumbai | Public Holidays in Mumbai | Mumbai AQI | Weather in Mumbai | Petrol Price in Mumbai | Diesel Price in Mumbai | CNG Price in Mumbai | LPG Price in MumbaiStay updated with the latest Mumbai news. articles.body: Brazilian TikToker Duda Alves has died at the age of 22, just days after sharing videos about her painful recovery from breast-reduction surgery. The creator, whose real name was Maria Eduarda Alves dos Santos, had more than 750,000 followers and 27 million likes on TikTok. Her family announced her death on September 15, two days after she passed away, according to People. Her death has led to questions about her final videos. However, her cause of death has not been made public, and no confirmed link to her surgery has been established.Brazilian TikToker Duda Alves dies at 22 as police investigate unexplained deathDuda Alves died on September 13, according to People. Her family shared the news publicly two days later. A wake for the TikToker was held at São João Paulo II Parish in Brasília on September 15.According to UOL, the cause of her death has not been disclosed. The Civil Police of Brazil’s Federal District are investigating the case but have not shared further details. Police also said they could not provide more information because of the family’s privacy.There is currently no confirmed evidence that connects Alves’ recent breast-reduction surgery to her death. Her final days have received attention because she had openly spoken about the difficult recovery process in her TikTok videos.Duda Alves’ final videos showed her painful surgery recoveryBefore her death, Duda Alves had been sharing updates about her recovery after breast-reduction surgery. UOL reported that she decided to have the procedure because she felt uncomfortable wearing workout clothes. She also felt that her breasts were not in proportion to her body.In a video posted on September 8, Alves said that around three weeks had passed since her surgery. She explained that she was experiencing “a lot of pain” during her recovery.The TikToker also said that she had been vomiting often and crying because of the pain. Her videos showed her talking about the challenges she faced after the procedure.Her final TikTok was posted on September 9. In the video, Alves responded to men who had criticised her decision to undergo breast-reduction surgery. She explained that she had chosen the procedure for both comfort and appearance.Duda was known for making funny videos about her daily life. She also had a recurring series where she listed things she disliked. Her content helped her build a large audience on TikTok.Following her death, friends and family members shared emotional tributes. Duda’s father also thanked people who supported his daughter during the wake.Duda Alves’ death at 22 has left her family, friends, and followers mourning. While her recent videos focused on her painful surgery recovery, her cause of death remains unknown, and authorities have not confirmed any connection between the surgery and her passing. The investigation continues as loved ones remember the Brazilian TikToker for her humour, personality, and online presence.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: ‘Absolutely no ambiguity: Pakistan says Mecca pact applies as Saudi Arabia faces Houthi drone threat
articles.summary: Pakistan News: Pakistan on Thursday said it was committed to implementing its defence agreement with Saudi Arabia and Turkiye amid escalating tensions in the Gulf re.
articles.body: Pakistan on Thursday said it was committed to implementing its defence agreement with Saudi Arabia and Turkiye amid escalating tensions in the Gulf region following what Riyadh described as an attempted Houthi drone attack near the Muslim holy city of Mecca.The trilateral Mecca defence agreement, signed by Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye last month, establishes a framework for collective deterrence and stipulates that an armed attack against any one of the three countries would be regarded as an attack against all.Pakistan defence minister Khawaja Asif said Islamabad was fully prepared to fulfil its obligations under the pact.“The Mecca Agreement applies to us, and we will fulfil our duty,” Asif was quoted as saying by Geo News.Also read| Mecca Pact, but no troops yet: Pakistan expresses 'solidarity' with Saudi Arabia after Houthi attacks on kingdomPakistan keeps military response details confidentialAsif’s comments came after Saudi authorities said their air defences had intercepted and destroyed a Houthi drone south of Mecca. The drone was destroyed before entering the city’s prohibited airspace, according to Saudi authorities.The Houthis denied targeting Mecca or any Islamic holy site.“If Mecca is attacked, there is no need for an agreement to protect it,” Asif was quoted as saying.He said Pakistan did not need a formal agreement to protect the Muslim holy sites and that safeguarding them was a duty even without the pact.During his weekly briefing on Thursday, Pakistan foreign office spokesperson Sajjad Haider Khan reiterated Islamabad’s commitment to implementing the agreement.Asked whether any mechanism had been devised for Pakistan to help thwart recent Houthi attacks in Saudi Arabia, Khan said Pakistan remained committed to “implementing” the agreement.“However, when, how, where and what force will be used against what objectives, in which modes and matters — operational confidentiality requires us to be discreet at this stage,” he said.Asif had also said on Wednesday that there was “absolutely no ambiguity” about the pact’s application if the territorial integrity or geographical boundaries of any of the three countries were violated.He stressed, however, that Pakistan would not publicly discuss its defence or military strategy.Saudi Arabia faces Houthi drone and missile threatThe latest tensions follow Saudi Arabia’s accusation that the Houthis attempted to target Mecca with a drone. The group denied the allegation.The attacks have also put the newly signed defence pact under scrutiny. Pakistan’s military has described the agreement as defensive and intended for collective deterrence, with “no regional aspirations”.Pakistan’s Inter-Services public relations chief Lt Gen Ahmed Sharif Chaudhry said the operational details of the pact were classified and would be decided by the three countries if the agreement were triggered.Also read| Pak scrambles to define Mecca pact after Houthi attackThe pact was signed on August 7 and states that an armed attack against any one of the three members would be regarded as an attack against all.Saudi Arabia had sought air-defence support from France, Britain, Pakistan and Egypt as it faced shortages of missile interceptors. However, officials from Pakistan and Turkiye told news agency AP that they had not received a Saudi request for military support in response to the latest Houthi escalation.Islamabad urges diplomacy, warns over Red SeaPakistan’s foreign office also highlighted the wider security risks from the conflict.Khan described the situation around Bab el-Mandeb as “exceptionally serious” and called on the Houthis to stop their activities.He said Pakistan had long advocated peace and stability in the region because “this is not only in the interest of Pakistan and Iran, but also the entire region and beyond.”“In this regard, our discussions basically revolve around bringing peace and stability through dialogue and diplomacy and not through coercive measures,” Khan said.Asif said Pakistan had conveyed Saudi Arabia’s message to Iran amid concerns over Houthi attacks against the kingdom.He said he did not think Iran as a state would open another front, while distinguishing between the Iranian government and non-state groups that could act without formal approval from a state.He said Pakistan would continue efforts to prevent the conflict from expanding into additional theatres.The defence minister also said disruptions to maritime routes, including the Strait of Hormuz and Bab el-Mandab, were affecting trade and economies across the region. He said the disruption was particularly important for Pakistan because of its impact on the country’s economy.Turkey’s defence ministry condemned the Houthi drone attack targeting Saudi Arabia and other actions by the group.The ministry said the continued Houthi threat in the Red Sea and Bab el-Mandab was negatively affecting regional security, international maritime trade and global stability.Pakistan Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Wednesday reiterated Pakistan’s full support for Saudi Arabia’s defence and said Islamabad stood “shoulder to shoulder” with Riyadh.Sharif condemned what he described as a “dastardly and heinous attempted drone attack” against the holy city and urged all parties to exercise maximum restraint and avoid further escalation.Catch the latest World News and Live updates.
